tasks.title: Implement DB schema/migrations
tasks.description: Create the item_categories, items, recipes, and recipe_inputs tables per the finalized data model.
tasks.notes: Added robmorgan/phinx as the migration tool (backend/phinx.php config, backend/db/migrations/). First migration 20260801141549_create_recipe_management_tables.php creates item_categories, items, recipes, recipe_inputs with NOT NULL/unique/FK constraints matching the schema decision (RESTRICT on category/item deletion while still referenced, CASCADE on recipe_inputs when their parent recipe is deleted). Verified by migrating against the running mysql container and inspecting DESCRIBE/SHOW CREATE TABLE output. Also added a file-based recipe data workflow: scripts/export-recipe-data.sh dumps recipe tables to backend/db/seeds/recipe_data.sql (the committed source of truth, not the Docker volume); a RecipeDataSeeder Phinx seed re-imports it; backend/docker-entrypoint.sh auto-runs migrate+seed on every container start with retry/backoff. Verified end-to-end via docker compose down -v + up. See key_decisions in project.json.

tasks.title: Implement recipe_type single source of truth + GET /recipe-types
tasks.description: Add the backend config file listing recipe types (t1_industry, t2_industry, reaction, pi) and a GET /recipe-types endpoint that serves it; POST /recipes validation reads from the same file.
tasks.notes: backend/config/recipe_types.php holds [{value, label}] for the 4 types. backend/src/RecipeTypes.php (new App\ PSR-4 namespace, added to composer.json autoload) reads it: all() for the GET endpoint, values()/isValid() for task #8's future POST /recipes validation to reuse. GET /recipe-types wired in public/index.php, verified via curl. Also uncovered and fixed a Docker gotcha: Compose preserves anonymous volumes across container recreate by default, so refreshing backend/vendor after a composer.json change needs `docker compose up -d --force-recreate --renew-anon-volumes backend`, not just a rebuild - recorded in project.json and README.

Verified all paths via curl against the running backend, including the FK-in-use 409.

notes.title: Implement items endpoints incl. resolve-by-name
notes.description: GET /items (filter by category_id + name search), GET /items/{id}, POST /items, PATCH /items/{id}, DELETE /items/{id} (reject if referenced by any recipe), GET /items/{id}/recipes, and POST /items/resolve (batch name lookup returning matched/unmatched).
notes.notes: backend/src/ItemsController.php: index (category_id + search filters), show, create, update (partial - only touches name/category_id keys present in the payload), delete (409 if referenced by recipes.product_item_id or recipe_inputs.input_item_id via FK RESTRICT), recipes (list recipes for a product item, for task #9's multi-recipe dropdown), resolve (batch name lookup, matched/unmatched per the API decision). category_id validated against item_categories via FK, invalid id surfaces as 422 not a raw DB error. Verified every path via curl including duplicate-name 409, invalid-category 422, partial-update semantics, delete-while-referenced 409, and resolve's matched/unmatched shape.

notes.title: Implement recipes endpoints
notes.description: GET /recipes (filter by recipe_type, product category_id, product name search), GET /recipes/{id} (incl. inputs), POST /recipes, PATCH /recipes/{id} (inputs replaced wholesale), DELETE /recipes/{id}. Enforce the multi-recipe rule: allowed if recipe_type is t2_industry, otherwise reject if a recipe already exists for that product.
notes.notes: backend/src/RecipesController.php: index (recipe_type/category_id/search filters, joins items for product name), show (incl. inputs with resolved input item names), create/update share a validate() method (product_item_id, recipe_type via RecipeTypes::isValid, variant_label/notes null-if-empty, output_quantity>=1, inputs non-empty with per-row validation - no self-referential input, no duplicate input_item_id) and a transactional write (recipe row + wholesale-replaced recipe_inputs, rolled back together on any failure). Multi-recipe rule implemented as: t2_industry creates/edits always allowed; any other type is rejected with 409 if any OTHER recipe already exists for that product_item_id (checked on both create and update, self-excluded on update) - confirmed this correctly allows a product to hold one non-t2 recipe alongside multiple t2 variants simultaneously, matching the decision's literal wording. delete cascades recipe_inputs via the existing FK. Extracted decodeBody/jsonError (previously duplicated in ItemCategoriesController and ItemsController) into a shared JsonResponseHelpers trait used by all three controllers. Verified extensively via curl: full CRUD, multi-recipe accept/reject in both directions, every validation error, list filters, and wholesale input replacement on PATCH.

notes.title: Implement frontend Recipe List page
notes.description: Table of recipes with recipe_type/category/name-search filters, Edit/Delete row actions, and a 'New Recipe' entry point.
notes.notes: Bare Angular scaffold had no HttpClient, routing, or components yet, so this task also laid the shared frontend plumbing: provideHttpClient() in app.config.ts; frontend/proxy.conf.json (dev-server proxies /api/* to http://backend:8000, wired via angular.json serve.options.proxyConfig) so the browser talks same-origin to localhost:4200 and never hits CORS (backend has no CORS middleware); models/recipe.model.ts (RecipeListItem, RecipeType, ItemCategory, RecipeFilters); services/recipes.service.ts, recipe-types.service.ts, item-categories.service.ts. Replaced the placeholder app.html with a minimal top nav (Recipes/Categories links) and added the /recipes route (root redirects to it) in app.routes.ts. RecipeList page (pages/recipe-list/): recipe_type dropdown (from GET /recipe-types) + category dropdown (from GET /item-categories) + product-name search input, all re-querying GET /recipes on change/Enter/Search-click; table of product/variant/type/output-qty with per-row Edit (routerLink-navigates to /recipes/{id}/edit, not implemented until task #10) and Delete (window.confirm then DELETE /recipes/{id} and reload); 'New Recipe' links to /recipes/new (task #10). Verified: `ng build` and `ng test` pass inside the running frontend container; confirmed the proxy end-to-end via curl (localhost:4200/api/recipe-types and a temporary POST'd item+recipe showed up via localhost:4200/api/recipes, then cleaned up). Could not visually verify the rendered page in a real browser - Claude in Chrome was not connected this session - so the user should open http://localhost:4200/recipes to confirm the UI looks/behaves as expected before relying on it.

notes.title: Implement frontend Recipe Form
notes.description: Shared create/edit form: recipe_type dropdown, product/input name fields with quantities, manual 'Check Items' resolve button, inline category picker + create button for unmatched items, and Save wired to POST/PATCH /recipes.
notes.notes: pages/recipe-form/ (RecipeForm), shared by routes recipes/new and recipes/:id/edit (added to app.routes.ts). Added ItemsService (resolve, create) and RecipesService.get/create/update. Each resolvable name (product + each input row) tracked client-side as {name, itemId, checked, matched, categoryId, categoryName}; editing a name text resets it to unresolved (must re-check). 'Check Items' sends one POST /items/resolve with [productName, ...inputNames] and zips the parallel results back by index. Unmatched entries show an inline category select (from GET /item-categories, 'No category' = null) + a 'Create' button -> POST /items, which resolves that entry in place. Save Recipe is disabled until product + every input row is matched; save() also re-checks the same rules the backend enforces (no self-referential input, no duplicate input_item_id, quantities >= 1, recipe_type/output_quantity set) so the user gets an immediate inline message instead of only a round-tripped 422/409 - the backend's own 409 (multi-recipe rule) and any other server error still surface via the error banner (parsed from the {error: message} body JsonResponseHelpers always returns). Edit mode (recipes/:id/edit) GETs the recipe and pre-seeds product/inputs as already-matched (server-given ids trusted) with quantities/variant_label/output_quantity/notes/recipe_type filled in; changing a pre-filled name still forces re-resolution. Verified: `ng build`/`ng test` pass in the running frontend container; curl-verified the exact request/response shapes the component sends and expects (resolve on unmatched names, create, POST /recipes, GET /recipes/{id}, PATCH /recipes/{id}) all match the RecipePayload/RecipeDetail/Item/ItemResolveResult TypeScript models byte-for-byte, then cleaned up the temporary test data. Did not visually exercise the form in a real browser (Claude in Chrome not connected this session) - user should walk through creating and editing a recipe at http://localhost:4200/recipes/new before relying on it.

notes.title: Implement frontend Categories page
notes.description: List item_categories with inline rename, delete (surfacing the backend's in-use rejection), and a 'New Category' input.
notes.notes: pages/categories/ (Categories component), routed at /categories (already linked from the top nav added in task #9). Extended ItemCategoriesService with create/update/delete (list already existed). Simple list: 'New Category' input+button at top (POST, then reload); each row has Rename (inline input replaces the name cell, Save/Cancel) and Delete (window.confirm then DELETE). No client-side duplicate-name or in-use pre-check - the page just surfaces whatever the backend's {error: message} body says (409 duplicate name on create/rename, 409 in-use on delete) via an error banner, same pattern as recipe-form's error handling. Verified: `ng build`/`ng test` pass in the running frontend container; curl-verified create/rename/delete request-response shapes match ItemCategory, and confirmed the in-use delete rejection returns the exact 409 + message the page displays (created a category, attached an item to it, verified delete was rejected, then cleaned up). Did not visually exercise the page in a real browser (Claude in Chrome not connected this session) - user should check http://localhost:4200/categories before relying on it.

notes.title: End-to-end test with example recipes
notes.description: Enter the Robotics and Tungsten Carbide example recipes through the app and confirm they persist across a restart.
notes.notes: User entered three recipes through the live UI (recipe list/form/categories pages all exercised together): Cormorant (t1_industry, Ship category, 4 mineral inputs), Robotics (pi, Planetary Industry Product category, 10 Consumer Electronics + 10 Mechanical Parts -> 3 Robotics - corrected from an initially wrong quantity I proposed), and Tungsten Carbide (reaction, Reaction Product/Material categories, 98 Rolled Tungsten Alloy + 98 Sulfuric Acid -> 10000 - a facility-bonus-adjusted per-run value, see project memory on fractional reaction quantities for why 98 isn't the 'base' game value). Ran scripts/export-recipe-data.sh to snapshot all 4 tables to backend/db/seeds/recipe_data.sql, then did a full `docker compose down -v` (wipes the mysql volume and anonymous frontend/backend volumes) + `docker compose up -d`, and confirmed via curl against every affected endpoint (GET /recipes, /item-categories, and /recipes/{id} for all 3 with full input lists) that ids, names, categories, and quantities came back byte-for-byte identical - the migrate+seed-on-startup flow in docker-entrypoint.sh correctly reconstructs schema and recipe data from the committed file alone. backend/db/seeds/recipe_data.sql is new and currently uncommitted - user should `git add`/commit it (and any future recipe additions need a re-export before they're durable, since the seeder truncates+reimports from that file on every backend container start).
